releases.name: 0.13.1 — review demos and search discoverability
releases.body:
# OpenCode Annotate 0.13.1

A documentation and discoverability update. Runtime behavior is unchanged from 0.13.0.

- A clearer README introduces terminal review for AI replies and Markdown, browser webpage annotation, and conversation references.
- Real terminal and Chrome-panel captures show selection and comments using synthetic demo content, with reproducible capture sources and documented limits.
- Updated package description and relevant keywords make the review workflows easier to identify. Search engines control recrawling and ranking; no ranking improvement is claimed.

## Install

```sh
opencode plugin add @nxxxsooo/opencode-annotate@latest
```

## Update

```sh
opencode plugin update @nxxxsooo/opencode-annotate@latest
```

Keep your existing plugin options. Publication does not update an installed copy automatically. Requires OpenCode 2.2.0+; the terminal reviewer is bundled. Browser setup is optional and separate; Safari is copy-only. Windows terminal handoff remains unverified.

The release passed the five-platform native build/test matrix, Safari build gate and npm package checks. Local verification also covered 98 Node tests, 21 isolated OpenCode smoke scenarios and the reference suite, without a model turn. The unchanged browser runtime passed 33 headless scenarios during demo capture.

[README and demos](https://github.com/nxxxsooo/opencode-annotate#readme) · [Changes](https://github.com/nxxxsooo/opencode-annotate/compare/v0.13.0...v0.13.1)

releases.name: 0.13.0 — auto-sizing reference comments
releases.body:
## Auto-sizing `/ref` comments

Add an optional comment when referencing another conversation. The field grows and
shrinks with your text, wraps long lines, and scrolls at a screen-aware height limit.
Multiline paste and Chinese text keep their line breaks.

- **Shift+Enter**: new line.
- **Enter**: continue to the existing attachment confirmation.
- **Esc** or **Ctrl+C**: cancel without attaching.

Comments are separate from quoted history. Reference delivery is unchanged: it queues
context for the next prompt and does not start an idle assistant. This release does not
include the development-only inline reference annotations, references from home,
automatic continuation, Chrome session picker, or command consolidation.

### Install

```sh
opencode plugin add @nxxxsooo/opencode-annotate@latest
```

### Update

```sh
opencode plugin update @nxxxsooo/opencode-annotate@latest
```

Keep one server-plus-TUI plugin entry in `opencode.json(c)` and preserve your existing
options. Run `/reload` if the command list has not refreshed. Optional toolbar artwork
remains local; Safari remains a copy-only companion distributed as source/build support.

Tested with OpenCode 2.2.7: 98 Node tests, Rust formatting/Clippy/workspace tests,
21 isolated OpenCode smoke scenarios, and reference-editor growth/shrink, multiline CJK
paste, Shift+Enter, bounded scrolling, terminal resizing and cancellation. Smoke checks
do not start a model turn.

releases.name: 0.12.0 — Safari companion and compact review toolbar
releases.body:
## Safari companion and compact review toolbar

- Safari companion: shared browser sources, a separate panel window, local annotation
  rounds and **Copy notes**. Safari does not deliver directly to OpenCode sessions;
  Chrome retains its existing pairing and delivery behavior.
- Four compact TUI actions: approve, comment, **Done** (Enter) and **Get** (`g`). Done
  records that the requested work is finished; Get records understanding. Esc dismisses.
- Optional user-supplied PNG toolbar artwork through Kitty graphics: one text row,
  action-colored bold shortcuts, cached images and clean removal. No Lark artwork is
  included. Unicode icons remain the default.
- Explicit copy now confirms **Copied to clipboard (N chars)**.

### Install or update

```sh
opencode plugin add @nxxxsooo/opencode-annotate@0.12.0
# Existing installations:
opencode plugin update @nxxxsooo/opencode-annotate@latest
```

Preserve existing plugin options and reload/reopen the terminal client afterward.
Checkout-based development installations must be updated separately.

### Safari distribution

This release includes **source and local build/install scripts**, not a downloadable
signed/notarized Safari app. Build with Xcode and your own appropriate Apple signing
identity, then run `npm run install:safari` and enable the extension in Safari Settings.
See the README for the complete signing/build steps and the copy-only limitation.

### Compatibility

- Node.js 22+, OpenCode 2.2+, Safari 18+ on macOS for the browser companion.
- PNG toolbar mode is explicit opt-in for verified Kitty-graphics terminals and local
  artwork. Multiplexers are not supported by this trial; font/DPI changes require
  remeasuring configured cell pixels.
- Existing commands, including `/annotate-web`, are retained. Unrelated unpublished
  reference, continuation and Chrome session-picker changes are not in this release.

releases.name: v0.11.1 — comment cursor movement
releases.body:
## Comment cursor movement

- **Up/Down** now move the cursor between wrapped rows in the comment and edit box. A long
  comment without line breaks used to let the cursor move only left and right.
- **Cmd+Left/Right** jump to the start or end of the line, **Cmd+Up/Down** to the start or
  end of the comment, and **Option+Left/Right** move by word. The Ctrl+A/Ctrl+E and
  Alt+B/Alt+F that macOS terminals send for these keys work the same way.

No options, key bindings or stored annotations change.

## Install or update

Requires OpenCode **2.2.0+**, Node **22+**. Native reviewers are included for macOS arm64/x64,
Linux arm64/x64 (glibc 2.35+), and Windows x64.

```sh
opencode plugin add @nxxxsooo/opencode-annotate@latest
# Existing installation:
opencode plugin update @nxxxsooo/opencode-annotate@latest
```

Run `/reload` or reopen OpenCode if the reviewer has not refreshed.

## Verification

Node tests, Rust formatting/Clippy/workspace tests and the package dry-run passed locally. A
headless terminal run of the built reviewer confirmed wrapped-row Up, Ctrl+A/Ctrl+E and
Alt+B. Release automation built native reviewers for all five targets and published with
signed provenance.

[Full changelog](https://github.com/nxxxsooo/opencode-annotate/compare/v0.11.0...v0.11.1)

releases.name: 0.11.0 — what? notes and explicit copy
releases.body:
## what? notes

- Select a passage you don't understand and press **`w`** (or click **❓ what?**). The review
  saves a short `what?` note, so the comment rail stays readable.
- When you send, the feedback adds one instruction after all the notes: explain each marked
  passage in plain language with more detail and a concrete example where it helps, relate
  it to the current task, and hold any pending action until you confirm.
- Change or remove that instruction with `[prompts] what` in
  `~/.config/opencode-annotate/tui.toml`; an empty string sends the notes alone.
- If OpenCode has a skill with ID `what`, the plugin attaches it to the sent feedback, the
  same as mentioning `@what`. Set the `whatSkill` plugin option to another skill ID, or to
  `false` to turn this off. A missing default skill is skipped; a missing skill you
  configured stops the send with an error and keeps the draft and `feedback.md`.

## Explicit copy

- Selecting text no longer overwrites your clipboard. Press **`y`** or click **⧉ copy** to copy
  the selected source; the selection stays for annotating.
- Toolbar options wrap onto a second row in narrow panes and stay clickable.

New key-binding actions are `what` and `copy` under `[keys]`. Stored annotations and
existing options are unchanged.

## Install or update

Requires OpenCode **2.2.0+**, Node **22+**. Native reviewers are included for macOS arm64/x64,
Linux arm64/x64 (glibc 2.35+), and Windows x64.

```sh
opencode plugin add @nxxxsooo/opencode-annotate@latest
# Existing installation:
opencode plugin update @nxxxsooo/opencode-annotate@latest
```

Run `/reload` or reopen OpenCode if the reviewer has not refreshed.

## Verification

Node tests, Rust formatting/Clippy/workspace checks and 21 isolated OpenCode smoke scenarios
passed locally. The skill attachment was checked against a live OpenCode server in an isolated
session without a model turn. Release automation built native reviewers for all five targets
and published with signed provenance.

[Full changelog](https://github.com/nxxxsooo/opencode-annotate/compare/v0.10.4...v0.11.0)
